objects.description: No custom data types are defined in this header. It only declares two functions within the goldleaf_compat namespace: version() and add(int,int). There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes to document.

functions.name: goldleaf_compat::version
functions.description: Returns a C-string representing the Goldleaf compatibility layer's version. Intended for display, logging, or feature-gating based on version. No further documentation is provided; assumed to be a non-owning, null-terminated string.
requirements: Do not modify the returned string (it is a const char*).
Do not attempt to free or delete the returned pointer (ownership is not transferred).
Treat the return as a null-terminated C string; encoding is unspecified (likely ASCII/UTF-8).
Return value nullability and lifetime are not documented; callers should defensively handle a potential null and avoid storing the pointer beyond immediate use unless library guarantees are known.

functions.name: goldleaf_compat::add
functions.description: Computes and returns the sum of two integers. Useful for simple arithmetic where int precision suffices. No additional behavior is documented.
requirements: Inputs a and b are regular int values; no special initialization is required.
Ensure that a + b does not overflow or underflow the range of int to avoid undefined behavior in C/C++ signed arithmetic.
No error reporting is defined; the function returns the computed sum directly.
